items.title: The top differential of the Hodge-to-de Rham page vanishes for a smooth proper equidimensional scheme over a field
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the differential on the top part of the Hodge-to-de Rham page vanishes for a smooth proper equidimensional scheme over a field, which is one of the two degeneration inputs to Poincare duality (statement lines 4576-4584). The proof first reduces to the case where the global functions equal the base field, then splits by characteristic: in characteristic $p$ it uses the relative Frobenius together with the Garel maps, finiteness of the Frobenius and Hodge duality to force the vanishing, while in characteristic $0$ it spreads the situation out to a smooth proper family over a finite type $\mathbf{Z}$-algebra, makes the cohomology finite free by localization, and reduces modulo a dense set of primes to the characteristic $p$ case. The two-case Frobenius and spreading-out argument is the substance, so the claim is H3.
